doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Joe Williams and the blues as the basis of jazz
summary: Roker says Williams can really sing the blues, and explains jazz as rooted in blues and Gospel feeling, including a happy kind of blues.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Tell us about Joe. How do you feel his voice typifies jazz vocals?
Because he can really sing the blues. And if you play jazz, if it doesn’t feel like the blues is involved, then it’s classical. You know what I’m saying? Jazz, the basics of jazz is the blues.

Right. You know the Gospel feelings, you know, even the greatest saxophone players, the greatest instrumentalists, they know how to put blues into their statements you know. Not to say that they’ve got to be playing blues like B.B. King, I mean just the feeling, the happy feeling of the blues.
Now that’s something I want you to talk about. You said “the happy feeling of the blues.” All right now elaborate on that.

Well you know the blues have many faces. Some people cry man the ol’ lady left ‘em and all that, but sometimes the blues can be happy man, because it’s a feeling man that generates the spirit of Christ, which makes you happy, you know what I mean? You’re saved. I mean you’re pure, it’s clean. So that type of blues is what I’m talking about you know. Like Milt Jackson, the way he plays the blues. It makes you want to jump up and dance you know, and so that’s happy. That kind of blues.
